repo.description:
## Summary

The better-auth `apiKey` plugin's own HTTP endpoint `POST /api/auth/api-key/create` is enabled. It accepts client-supplied `metadata`, and Dokploy trusts `metadata.organizationId` to pick the organization context for the key. The tRPC wrapper `user.createApiKey` checks that the caller is a member of that organization; the native endpoint does not. Any authenticated user can mint a key bound to an organization they do not belong to. `validateRequest` then builds a session with `activeOrganizationId` set to that organization and `role` defaulting to `"member"` even though no membership row exists. Every `protectedProcedure` that scopes data only by `ctx.session.activeOrganizationId` then serves the foreign organization's data.

## Affected version

- Verified on: Dokploy v0.30.10 (self-hosted)
- Code unchanged on `canary` at d64ebedd0

## Code

- `packages/server/src/lib/auth.ts:488-491`: `apiKey({ enableMetadata: true, references: "user" })`, and `/api-key/*` is not in `disabledPaths` (`auth.ts:73-83`).
- `packages/server/src/lib/auth.ts:592-635`: `organizationId` taken from key metadata; `member` lookup may return null; `role: member?.role || "member"` (line 634) and `activeOrganizationId: organizationId` are set regardless.
- Example data endpoint: `apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/tag.ts:50-57` (`tag.all`, `protectedProcedure`, filters only by `activeOrganizationId`).

## Preconditions

- Attacker has any account on the instance (here: a plain member of organization B only).
- Attacker knows the victim organization id (org ids are not secret in the sense of being access-controlled; how hard they are to obtain was not assessed).

## Reproduction (local test instance only)

```
# user B: member of "E2E Second Org" only, not a member of "My Organization" (<orgA>)
curl -s -b memberB.jar -H "origin: http://127.0.0.1:13000" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"x","metadata":{"organizationId":"<orgA>"}}' \
  http://127.0.0.1:13000/api/auth/api-key/create
# -> {"id":"...","key":"<key>","metadata":{"organizationId":"<orgA>"},...}

# control: the tRPC path rejects the same request
curl ... -d '{"name":"x","metadata":{"organizationId":"<orgA>"}}' http://127.0.0.1:13000/api/user.createApiKey
# -> 403 "You are not a member of this organization"

# owner of orgA creates a tag "sec-canary-tag-myorg"; then, with B's foreign key:
curl -s -H "x-api-key: <key>" http://127.0.0.1:13000/api/tag.all
```

## Observed result

- Native endpoint returned a key with `metadata.organizationId = <orgA>`.
- `tag.all` with that key returned orgA's tag (`sec-canary-tag-myorg`, `organizationId: <orgA>`). B's own session returns `[]` for `tag.all`.
- Procedures that call `checkPermission`/`findMemberByUserId` (e.g. `project.all`, `server.all`) returned `Permission denied`, so exposure is limited to procedures that rely on `activeOrganizationId` alone.
- Native keys get better-auth's default rate limit (10 requests / 24h per key), but the attacker can mint new keys at will.

## Impact

Confirmed on a fresh v0.30.10 instance with a key minted this way (attacker = plain member of org B only):

- Read: `tag.all` (victim tags), `customRole.membersByRole?roleName=owner|admin|member` (every victim member's email, first/last name, userId), `organization.active` (victim org row).
- Write: `network.create` inserted a network row into the victim org and created a real Docker network on the host (`docker network ls` shows it). Source review shows `network.remove/recreate/resync/import` are reachable the same way (not exercised).
- From source review only (not exercised): git providers the victim shared with the org are listed by `gitProvider.getAll` / `github.githubProviders` etc., and `github.getGithubRepositories` / `gitlab.getGitlabRepositories` / `gitea.*` / `bitbucket.*` would use the victim's provider credentials to list private repos and branches.
- Procedures that look up the member row (`withPermission`, `checkPermission`, `findMemberByUserId`, e.g. `project.all`, `server.all`, env vars, apps, databases) return "Permission denied", so exposure is limited to `protectedProcedure`s that scope only by `activeOrganizationId`.

## Suggested fix (tested)

1. Add `/api-key/create` and `/api-key/update` to `disabledPaths`, as done for SCIM in GHSA-j8v8-g9cx-5qf4. Keys are created via tRPC `user.createApiKey`, which calls `auth.createApiKey` server-side and is unaffected.
2. In `validateRequest`, reject the key when no `member` row exists for `(key.userId, metadata.organizationId)` instead of defaulting `role` to `"member"`. This also kills keys already minted this way, and keys of users later removed from the org.

Patch against `canary` d64ebedd0:

```diff
diff --git a/packages/server/src/lib/auth.ts b/packages/server/src/lib/auth.ts
index e07693d35..8acd8be77 100644
--- a/packages/server/src/lib/auth.ts
+++ b/packages/server/src/lib/auth.ts
@@ -80,6 +80,10 @@ const createBetterAuth = () =>
 			"/scim/list-provider-connections",
 			"/scim/get-provider-connection",
 			"/scim/delete-provider-connection",
+			// API keys are minted via tRPC (user.createApiKey), which checks org membership.
+			// The native routes accept client-set metadata.organizationId.
+			"/api-key/create",
+			"/api-key/update",
 			...(!IS_CLOUD ? ["/verify-email"] : []),
 		],
 		secret: betterAuthSecret,
@@ -611,6 +615,13 @@ export const validateRequest = async (request: IncomingMessage) => {
 				},
 			});
 
+			if (!member) {
+				return {
+					session: null,
+					user: null,
+				};
+			}
+
 			// When accessing from DB, use actual column names
 			const userFromDb = apiKeyRecord.user as typeof apiKeyRecord.user & {
 				firstName: string;
@@ -631,8 +642,8 @@ export const validateRequest = async (request: IncomingMessage) => {
 					createdAt: userFromDb.createdAt,
 					updatedAt: userFromDb.updatedAt,
 					twoFactorEnabled: userFromDb.twoFactorEnabled,
-					role: member?.role || "member",
-					ownerId: member?.organization.ownerId || apiKeyRecord.user.id,
+					role: member.role,
+					ownerId: member.organization.ownerId,
 					enableEnterpriseFeatures: userFromDb.enableEnterpriseFeatures,
 					isValidEnterpriseLicense: userFromDb.isValidEnterpriseLicense,
 				},
```

Verified by building v0.30.10 with the equivalent patch and upgrading the vulnerable instance in place: native `/api/auth/api-key/create` and `/update` return 404; a cross-org key minted before the upgrade returns 401; legitimate keys (pre-existing and newly created via `user.createApiKey`), session auth, `project.all`, `network.create` in the user's own org, and `user.deleteApiKey` keep working.
repo.summary: Cross-organization API key via better-auth /api/auth/api-key/create (client-set metadata.organizationId)
